It's easy to earn Aeroplan points — even if you live in the U.S. — since the program partners with most major transferable points and miles programs, so you can earn Aeroplan points with your everyday spending. Here is everything you need to know about Air Canada Aeroplan. Related: Why Air Canada Aeroplan has become my favorite Star Alliance loyalty program Aeroplan pros and cons Pros - There are published award charts with low redemption rates for most partner airlines. - No carrier-imposed surcharges apply. - You can enjoy one stopover per direction of travel, including on one-way tickets, for 5,000 extra points. - Transfer partnerships with most major transferable rewards programs are available, all at a 1:1 ratio. - You can pool points with up to eight family members, and credit card preferred pricing is shared across the pool. - Generous lap infant pricing is available, and there's no fare within Canada or between Canada and the U.S. Cons - Air Canada's own flights are priced dynamically and can be extremely high on busy dates. - Change and cancellation fees are steep. - Complex stopover itineraries often have to be booked by phone, which carries its own fee. - Points expire after 18 months without activity. - Partner premium cabin availability can be hard to find. Air Canada Aeroplan partners Air Canada is part of Star Alliance, the world's biggest airline alliance. You can earn and redeem Aeroplan points on any Star Alliance airline, making it easy to get just about anywhere in the world. You'll find Star Alliance hubs in some of the world's largest airports, including Chicago's O'Hare International Airport (ORD), Frankfurt Airport (FRA), Istanbul Airport (IST) and Tokyo's Haneda Airport (HND). The following airlines are Star Alliance members: - Aegean Airlines - Air Canada - Air China - Air India - Air New Zealand - All Nippon Airways - Asiana Airlines - Austrian Airlines - Avianca - Brussels Airlines - Copa Airlines - Croatia Airlines - Egyptair - Ethiopian Airlines - EVA Air - ITA Airways - LOT Polish Airlines - Lufthansa - Shenzhen Airlines - Singapore Airlines - South African Airways - Swiss - TAP Air Portugal - Thai Airways - Turkish Airlines - United Airlines Aeroplan also has partnerships with many carriers outside of Star Alliance, including: - Aer Lingus (codeshare only) - AirBaltic - Air Creebec - Air Dolomiti - Air Inuit - Air Mauritius - Air Serbia - Azul Brazilian Airlines - Bamboo Airways - Bearskin Airlines - Calm Air - Canadian North - Cathay Pacific (select routes only) - Central Mountain Air (codeshare only) - Discover Airlines - Edelweiss Air (codeshare only) - Emirates - Etihad Airways - Eurowings - Flydubai - Gol Airlines - Gulf Air - Harbour Air - Helijet - Juneyao Air (Star Alliance connecting partner) - Lufthansa City Airlines - Middle East Airlines (codeshare only) - Olympic Air - Oman Air - PAL Airlines - SriLankan Airlines (codeshare only) - SunExpress - Virgin Australia Be sure to review the information on Air Canada's airline partner page to understand the full scope of each carrier's partnership. For example, as noted, some of the airlines listed above only have codeshare partnerships with Air Canada; other partnerships — such as Cathay Pacific — are limited to specific routes. Air Canada Aeroplan elite status Air Canada Aeroplan rewards its frequent flyers with valuable perks like seat upgrade certificates, free checked bags and other benefits across five different status tiers. Likewise, Air Canada elite members receive reciprocal benefits on Star Alliance partner airlines. Earning Air Canada Aeroplan elite status Aeroplan recently changed how you qualify for elite status. It used to require earning a combination of Status Qualifying Miles, Status Qualifying Segments and Status Qualifying Dollars to earn status. Nowadays, the airline awards elite status solely on the number of Status Qualifying Credits you earn in a single calendar year. SQCs are earned based on how much you spend on an Air Canada flight or vacation package: - Economy Flex or higher: 4 SQCs per Canadian dollar spent - Economy Standard fares and eUpgrade add-ons: 2 SQCs per Canadian dollar spent - Air Canada Vacations packages: 1 SQC per Canadian dollar spent You can also earn 1 SQC for every 5 Aeroplan points earned with most partners, including Star Alliance partner airlines, up to 25,000 SQCs per year. For example, earning 10,000 Aeroplan points on a partner flight would also earn 2,000 SQCs. Exclusions apply for Aeroplan eStore earnings, bonus points and points converted from hotel or credit card programs. Additionally, nonalliance partner airlines do not earn SQCs. Here's a look at the requirements for each status tier: - Aeroplan 25K: 25,000 SQCs - Aeroplan 35K: 35,000 SQCs - Aeroplan 50K: 50,000 SQCs - Aeroplan 75K: 75,000 SQCs - Aeroplan Super Elite: 125,000 SQCs You can also earn Aeroplan 25K status by earning 100,000 Everyday Status Qualification points in a single calendar year. You'll earn 1 ESQ for every 1 eligible Aeroplan point earned with Aeroplan partners. This includes the Aeroplan eStore but excludes bonus miles and point conversions. Earning status with Aeroplan credit cards The Chase Air Canada Aeroplan® Credit Card (see rates and fees) can be a big help when earning Aeroplan elite status. That's because it includes automatic Aeroplan 25K elite status for as long as you have the card. Plus, you can upgrade to Aeroplan 35K status by spending $75,000 on your card in a given calendar year. Cardmembers can also earn up to 25,000 SQCs per calendar year with the Aeroplan card. It includes 5,000 SQCs as an annual bonus, 10,000 SQCs after spending $25,000 on your card in a calendar year and another 10,000 SQCs after spending $50,000. Aeroplan elite status requirements The higher your status, the more benefits you can enjoy when flying with Air Canada and its partner airlines. Below you'll find an overview of the Core Benefits awarded at each status level. You can also earn additional benefits when you earn Milestone Benefits, which we outline in the next section. Aeroplan 25K - Priority airport check-in, when available - Priority standby - Priority boarding with Air Canada, United and Lufthansa - Ability to earn 2 points per dollar spent on Air Canada-ticketed flights - Two complimentary checked bags on Air Canada flights - Complimentary handling of sports equipment - Preferred seat selection at check-in on eligible Air Canada routes - Avis Preferred Plus status match - Five eUpgrade credits - Star Alliance Silver status Aeroplan 35K All Aeroplan 25K benefits, plus: - Priority baggage handling on Air Canada flights - Priority security screening, where available - One extra complimentary checked bag on Air Canada flights - Ability to earn 3 points per dollar spent on Air Canada-ticketed flights - 10 eUpgrade credits Aeroplan 50K All Aeroplan 35K benefits, plus: - Access to Maple Leaf lounges and Air Canada cafes - Access to Virgin Australia lounges when flying Air Canada or Virgin Australia - Access to Emirates business-class lounges in Dubai when flying between Canada and Dubai - Preferred seat assignment at booking for Canada and U.S. routes on eligible Air Canada flights - Preferred seat assignment at check-in for other routes - Marriott Bonvoy Gold Elite status match - Ability to earn 4 points per dollar spent on Air Canada-ticketed flights - 15 eUpgrade credits - Star Alliance Gold status, which includes partner lounge access Aeroplan 75K All Aeroplan 50K benefits, plus: - Preferred seat selection at booking on all eligible Air Canada fares - Ability to earn 5 points per dollar spent on Air Canada-ticketed flights - 20 eUpgrade credits Aeroplan Super Elite All Aeroplan 75K benefits, plus: - Access to the Arrivals Lounge in Terminal 2 of London's Heathrow Airport (LHR) - Complimentary changes and cancellations on Aeroplan award tickets - Complimentary inflight refreshments in economy - Two status passes to share elite perks with a friend for a single itinerary - Gift your eUpgrade credits to someone else - Avis President's Club status match - Ability to earn 6 points per dollar spent on Air Canada-ticketed flights - 30 eUpgrade credits Milestone Benefits Milestone Benefits provides another way for Air Canada frequent flyers to earn eUpgrade credits (which can be used for flight upgrades) and other perks. Members start unlocking Milestone Benefits after earning 10,000 SQCs. You can pick benefits at some levels, with choices ranging from Maple Leaf Lounge passes to bonus points, status passes to share with friends and discounts on award tickets. How to earn Air Canada Aeroplan points It's surprisingly easy to earn Air Canada Aeroplan points, even if you're not flying Air Canada. Here's a look at some of the ways to earn them. Fly with Air Canada You'll earn Aeroplan points based on how much you spend on your Air Canada flight, with elite members earning bonus points. Members without elite status earn 1 point per dollar spent, and elite members can earn up to 6 points per dollar spent. Note that this is calculated based on your ticket price before taxes, fees and third-party charges. | Elite level | Points earned per dollar spent | |---|---| | Member (no elite status) | 1 | | Aeroplan 25K | 2 | | Aeroplan 35K | 3 | | Aeroplan 50K | 4 | | Aeroplan 75K | 5 | | Aeroplan Super Elite | 6 | Earning rates are based on the ticket cost in Canadian dollars. If you pay in a different currency, Air Canada will convert the cost of your ticket to Canadian dollars using an "industry-standard exchange rate" before calculating your earnings. Fly with Star Alliance and nonalliance partners Partner flights still earn Aeroplan points based on the distance flown and the fare class you book. Every partner airline's earning rates chart is listed on Air Canada's airline partner page. Find your partner airline on the list, and click on it. Here's how this works. Say you book a one-way United flight from Newark Liberty International Airport (EWR) to Chicago's O'Hare International Airport (ORD) on United's website, and your ticket is booked in D-fare domestic first class. According to Aeroplan's United earning chart, this ticket earns 150% of the miles flown. This flight clocks in at 719 miles, meaning you'd earn 1,079 Aeroplan points. Earn points with the Air Canada Aeroplan Credit Card Air Canada offers multiple credit cards in Canada and one here in the U.S. New Chase Air Canada Aeroplan Credit Card applicants can earn up to 115,000 bonus Aeroplan points: 75,000 bonus points after spending $4,000 on purchases in the first three months from account opening, plus an additional 40,000 bonus points after spending $20,000 on purchases in the first 12 months from account opening. In our September 2026 valuations, TPG values Aeroplan points as worth 1.5 cents each, making this welcome bonus worth $1,725. Know, though, that such a valuable welcome bonus comes with an annual fee of $195. With elevated earning rates in multiple categories (most notably, up to 5 points per dollar spent on Air Canada flights made with the card as an Aeroplan 25K elite member), plus up to $100 in annual Air Canada statement credits (up to two $50 semiannual credits), a 15% award discount when booking an itinerary with at least one Air Canada-operated flight and complimentary Aeroplan 25K elite status, this card is incredibly valuable, especially if you ever fly Air Canada. Transfer credit card points to Aeroplan You can transfer the following credit card rewards to Aeroplan at a 1:1 transfer ratio: - American Express Membership Rewards points - Bilt Points - Capital One miles - Chase Ultimate Rewards points This makes it easy to earn Aeroplan points on your everyday spending, as many transferable points and miles credit cards offer bonus points or miles on everyday purchases and large welcome bonuses. The following cards all currently offer strong welcome bonuses with points or miles that you can transfer to your Aeroplan account: You'll sometimes even find limited-time transfer bonuses when transferring points to Aeroplan. Related: Why transferable points and miles are worth more than other rewards Earn Aeroplan points at airport shops and restaurants Aeroplan added Club Avolta, which includes airport retail brands Hudson and Dufry, as an earning partner on June 30. Members who link their Aeroplan and Club Avolta accounts in the Club Avolta app earn 1 Aeroplan point for every CA$2 spent in store and on preorders placed through Avolta's Reserve & Collect service. More than 900 Avolta locations take part. In Canada, that includes Toronto Pearson Airport (YYZ), Vancouver International Airport (YVR) in British Columbia, Calgary International Airport (YYC) in Alberta and Billy Bishop Toronto City Airport (YTZ). In the U.S., it includes Los Angeles International Airport (LAX), San Francisco International Airport (SFO) and ORD. Avolta says the partnership will extend to its HMSHost dining outlets before the end of 2026, taking the network to close to 1,900 airport retail and food-and-beverage locations across North America. Earn with retail partners Air Canada has an online shopping portal that lets you earn Aeroplan points through third-party vendors such as Apple and Uber Eats. You can click through the merchant's link on the Air Canada eStore before you make a purchase and earn a set number of points per dollar spent. This can be a great way to earn bonus points on everyday purchases. However, not all Air Canada retail partners are valid for points-earning purchases in both the U.S. and Canada. Some are limited to Canada, so double-check your merchant's terms and conditions before using the eStore. Air Canada for Business Air Canada has a business rewards program called Air Canada for Business. Businesses can use this program to earn additional Aeroplan points on every flight and get a 5% discount on Flex fares and higher. Additionally, companies using Air Canada for Business earn 500 SQCs for every $5,000 spent on eligible fares. These SQCs can be allocated to employees, helping them reach a higher tier of elite status. Do Aeroplan points expire? Aeroplan points expire after 18 months of inactivity. Air Canada suspended that policy during the coronavirus pandemic and has extended the suspension several times since. Points that would otherwise have expired are protected through Nov. 29, and the standard policy returns the following day. Any earning or redeeming activity resets the clock on your entire balance, so a single small transaction protects a 500,000-point account as effectively as a 5,000-point one. Qualifying activity includes crediting a paid Air Canada or Star Alliance flight to your account, converting points from a credit card program, booking a hotel or car rental through Aeroplan, shopping through the Aeroplan eStore and redeeming for any Aeroplan reward. Members with Aeroplan elite status are exempt, as are primary cardholders of an Aeroplan cobranded credit card. Aeroplan Family Sharing Aeroplan lets up to eight verified family members pool their points into a single shared balance while keeping their individual accounts. Spouses and partners, children, siblings, in-laws, parents and grandparents can all join. The member who creates the pool is the family lead, who must be 18 or older and must have held an Aeroplan account for at least six months. Every point each member earns goes into the shared balance, including the points they already hold, and members cannot contribute only part of a balance. The family lead decides which members can redeem from the pool and which can only contribute to it. Redemptions come out of every member's account proportionally rather than from one person's balance, and any member with redemption privileges can book a reward for anyone, including someone outside the pool. If one member of the pool is the primary cardholder of an Aeroplan credit card, everyone in the pool sees that cardholder's preferred pricing on Aeroplan flight rewards, which can save thousands of points on a single booking. How to redeem Air Canada Aeroplan points You can use your Aeroplan points to fly worldwide; Air Canada offers a bevy of routes of its own, but its extensive alliance and nonalliance partner network expands this list even further. The program uses a standard award chart for most partner flights, pricing flights based on region and distance. However, Air Canada's own flights and those operated by select partners — including United, Emirates and Etihad — are priced dynamically. This means you can book many partner award flights at a predictable price. Aeroplan doesn't add fuel surcharges to award tickets, so you'll only pay minimal taxes, plus a CA$39 (about $28.70) partner booking fee (if applicable). Aeroplan's award chart As mentioned, Aeroplan employs a hybrid distance- and region-based award chart. You'll pay based on your flight length, but pricing varies based on the region you fly to and from. Each region is broadly defined. To find the cost of an award ticket booked by a nondynamic partner, first determine the regions you're flying from and to. Then, calculate the distance between your origin and destination using a tool like Great Circle Mapper. Next, find the award chart for your region pair in the Air Canada award chart to determine the cost of your flight. You can also search for your flight on Air Canada's website to view the price, as most partners are bookable online. Here is the chart for travel from North America to the Atlantic region, which includes flights from the U.S. to Europe. Flights on Brussels Airlines are priced based on the "All other partners" rates above, meaning they're based on the standard award chart. As such, a flight from New York's John F. Kennedy International Airport (JFK) to Brussels Airport (BRU) is 3,650 miles long, meaning it'd cost 60,000 points plus taxes and fees in business class. Things get trickier with Air Canada flights and those operated by the "select partners" that Aeroplan prices dynamically. This includes flights operated by United, Emirates, Flydubai, Etihad, Canadian North, Calm Air and Bearskin Airlines. In these instances, the figures listed on the award chart serve as a floor; you'll have to check Air Canada's website to find award costs for these airlines, and pricing can vary radically day to day, especially on Air Canada flights. Aeroplan award fees, changes and cancellations Air Canada does not charge a booking fee when you book a flight reward on its website. Booking through the Aeroplan Contact Center costs CA$30 per ticket, and that fee is nonrefundable and still applies when an itinerary cannot be completed online. Any award that includes a flight operated by a partner airline incurs an additional CA$39 partner booking fee per ticket. Change and cancellation fees depend on the fare option you book rather than the cabin, so a flexible economy award can be cheaper to cancel than a lowest-price business-class award. Same-day changes at the airport are priced separately. Changes and cancellations must be made at least two hours before departure. Booking awards for infants and children An infant under 2 at the time of travel who does not occupy a seat still needs their own ticket, but what that ticket costs depends on where you are going. For travel wholly within Canada and for travel between Canada and the U.S., no fare applies. For every other itinerary, including flights between the U.S. and Europe, Asia or South America, the fare is CA$25 or 2,500 Aeroplan points per direction of travel. Taxes, fees and charges still apply on top. Only one lap infant is permitted per adult traveling. The best ways to redeem Air Canada Aeroplan points The Aeroplan award chart is full of interesting sweet spots and great deals. Here are some of the best ways to maximize the award chart and the program's interesting features, such as stopovers on one-way award tickets. Book Air Canada flights on off-peak dates Aeroplan's system for dynamically pricing Air Canada-operated flights is unpredictable, but it can still lead to good deals on off-peak dates. This is especially true for short-haul cross-border and Canadian domestic flights, which are frequently priced at under 10,000 points one-way. Just note that fees can be high on cross-border flights, so make sure to compare the cost of an award ticket to buying a ticket outright. Meanwhile, on peak dates, the prices are often unreasonably high and not a great redemption option. This is especially true for flights from North America to Europe and Asia. However, if you are willing to travel on off-peak dates, you might be able to find a good deal on longer flights. Try booking seasonal flights in the first and last month of the season (you can use Air Canada's Wikipedia page to check which destinations are seasonal) for attractive pricing on low-demand dates. Book a mini round-the-world trip with stopovers You can add one stopover to one-way tickets or two stopovers to round-trip tickets for 5,000 points apiece. These stopovers can be anywhere in the world, and Aeroplan lets you get creative with your routing. The only major restriction to know is that your total distance flown can't exceed twice the nonstop distance to your destination. Stopovers are not permitted within Canada, the U.S. or China, and no stopover can run longer than 45 days. You can make some interesting itineraries with Aeroplan's flexible routing rules. For example, you can book a mini round-the-world trip that includes two stopovers and multiple 24-hour layovers. You can book stopover tickets online, but you may need to call to book more complex itineraries with additional layovers. If you choose to book a complicated itinerary with long layovers, make sure to find award space on Air Canada's website before you call to book. Related: The complete guide to Aeroplan's stopover and routing rules Fly partner airlines from the East Coast to Europe Many flights from the East Coast to Western Europe fall into the 0 to 4,000 miles tier on the North America-to-Atlantic award chart, and there are plenty of partner airlines flying across the Atlantic that regularly release seats to Aeroplan. This includes popular airlines like Austrian Airlines, Brussels Airlines, Lufthansa, LOT Polish Airlines, Swiss and TAP Air Portugal. These flights cost just 60,000 points in business class (Lufthansa recently stopped releasing first-class seats to partners like Aeroplan), so they're a great way to cross the Atlantic in style. If you're eyeing a longer flight to Europe, business-class flights cost 75,000 points for itineraries up to 6,000 miles. These options are cheaper than those offered by other Star Alliance programs, such as Avianca Lifemiles and United MileagePlus, for the same flights. Fly business class to India for 85,000 points You can book Star Alliance partners like United, Air India and Turkish Airlines between the U.S. and India for just 85,000 points each way in business class or 50,000 points each way in economy class. Bottom line Air Canada's Aeroplan loyalty program is great. Solid redemption rates, flexible stopovers and no fuel surcharges mean you can get some excellent deals on award tickets. The program also partners with many of the largest transferable points and miles programs, so it's easy to rack up Aeroplan points through your everyday spending. Even if you aren't planning to visit Canada or fly on Air Canada, you should consider the program for your next points transfer or major redemption. TPG featured card | 4X | Earn 4X Membership Rewards® points per dollar spent on purchases at restaurants worldwide, on up to $50,000 in purchases per calendar year, then 1X points for the rest of the year. | | 4X | Earn 4X Membership Rewards® points per dollar spent at US supermarkets, on up to $25,000 in purchases per calendar year, then 1X points for the rest of the year. | | 5X | Earn 5X Membership Rewards® points on prepaid hotel stays booked through AmexTravel.com or the Amex Travel App™. | | 3X | Earn 3X Membership Rewards® points on flights booked through AmexTravel.com, the Amex Travel App™, or purchased directly from airlines. | | 2X | Earn 2X Membership Rewards® points on prepaid car rentals booked through AmexTravel.com or the Amex Travel App™ and cruises booked and paid through AmexTravel.com. | | 1X | Earn 1X Membership Rewards® point per dollar spent on all other eligible purchases. |

item.title: Who's eligible for the Chase Ink Business Cash and Unlimited's $1,000 cash-back welcome offer?
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy Score: 5.44
Who's eligible for the Chase Ink Business Cash and Unlimited's $1,000 cash-back welcome offer? If your small business is looking for an affordable way to earn cash back or boost its Ultimate Rewards balance, the Ink Business Cash® Credit Card (see rates and fees) and Ink Business Unlimited® Credit Card (see rates and fees) are two great choices. Currently, both cards are offering their highest-ever welcome bonuses, which could be even more valuable if you have an eligible Ultimate Rewards card that provides access to Chase's transfer partners. It's important to know whether or not you're eligible for a welcome bonus. You don't want to waste a hard pull on your credit just to find out you didn't meet Chase's requirements from the start. Current offers on the Ink Business Cash and Ink Business Unlimited Currently, the Ink Business Cash and Ink Business Unlimited have the same welcome offer: Earn $1,000 bonus cash back after spending $8,000 on purchases in the first four months of account opening. These best-ever offers end on Sept. 17 at 9 a.m. ET, so I recommend applying sooner rather than later. We haven't seen offers this good on either of these cards before. According to TPG's September 2026 valuations, this welcome offer could be worth up to $2,050 if you hold a card that offers access to Chase's transfer partners, such as the Ink Business Preferred® Credit Card (see rates and fees) or the Chase Sapphire Reserve for Business℠ (see rates and fees). That's because you can combine the rewards you earn on your Ink Business Cash or Ink Business Unlimited with that account and redeem them with any of Chase's partners. Am I eligible for the Ink Business Cash or Ink Business Unlimited's welcome bonus? When considering whether you're eligible for a welcome bonus on either card, there are several factors to keep in mind. Chase 5/24 rule Chase's well-known 5/24 rule states that you may not be approved for a new Chase card if you've opened five or more personal credit cards over the past 24 months. While small-business cards like the Ink Business Cash and Ink Business Unlimited don't count toward 5/24, Chase will still take that rule into consideration when deciding whether to approve you. No-annual-fee Ink family rules Chase has gradually tightened its eligibility rules for cards in the same family. For the Ink Cash and Ink Unlimited, you can earn a welcome offer on either card, but not both. That rings true even if you earned a welcome bonus on one of these cards before the rules changed, or if you closed your account years ago. In addition, you likely won't be able to earn a second bonus on the same no-annual-fee Ink card. For example, if you previously earned a welcome bonus on the Ink Unlimited, you probably can't earn another one on that card. Do I need a business to open the Ink Cash or Ink Unlimited? You don't need a traditional business, such as an LLC, to open a small-business card like the Ink Cash or Ink Unlimited. However, you do need a side hustle or similar gig at a minimum. Freelancing, pet sitting, driving for a ride-hailing service and reselling are all examples of work that may qualify you for a small-business card. Related: How to get a business credit card Can I hold both the Ink Cash and Ink Unlimited at the same time? Yes, but remember that you likely won't be able to earn a welcome bonus on both cards. Since both cards have identical welcome offers right now, you don't need to worry about which card offers greater value with its bonus when deciding which to apply for first. If you don't want to hold both cards, your choice will come down to how your business typically spends. Since the Ink Business Cash earns bonus rewards at office supply stores and on common utilities, dining and gas (dining and gas subject to a spending cap), it's a better choice for business owners who frequently make those purchases. The Ink Business Unlimited earns 5% cash back on Lyft (through Sept. 30, 2027) and 1.5% cash back on all other purchases. That makes it an ideal choice for businesses that make a wide variety of purchases or whose spending habits shift regularly. Bottom line It's always important to check whether you're eligible for a card and its welcome bonus before applying. Credit card issuers will almost always perform a hard pull on your credit report when you apply; too many hard pulls on your credit report can lower your credit score. Given that, you don't want to waste a hard pull on a card you more than likely aren't eligible for. That said, if you meet the eligibility requirements for either the Ink Business Cash or Ink Business Unlimited, now is a great time to apply. Both of these cards have a best-ever welcome offer that's ending on Sept. 17 at 9 a.m. ET. To learn more, check out our full reviews of the Ink Business Cash and Ink Business Unlimited. Apply here: Chase Ink Business Cash Apply here: Chase Ink Business Unlimited

item.title: Ultimate guide to the Hilton Honors loyalty program
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy Score: 5.01
Ultimate guide to the Hilton Honors loyalty program Editor's Note - Hilton Honors is one of the largest hotel loyalty programs in the world, with more than 9,000 properties. - While not the most valuable hotel points, Hilton points are easy to earn and redeem, with frequent promotions, bonuses and redemption options beyond stays. - Hilton Diamond status can be yours with the right credit card. Hilton Honors is one of the largest hotel loyalty programs, with over 9,000 participating properties across 27 brands. I appreciate that the program offers excellent opportunities to earn Hilton points, valuable cobranded credit cards and multiple pathways to secure elite status. Although Hilton Honors isn't my primary hotel loyalty program, I maintain Hilton elite status through a cobranded credit card and stay at Hilton properties at least quarterly to maximize the up to $50 per quarter Hilton statement credit available through The Business Platinum Card® from American Express (enrollment is required; separate Hilton for Business enrollment is also required). So, whether you stay at Hilton properties weekly or annually, here's what you should know about the Hilton Honors program. What is Hilton Honors? Hilton Honors is the hotel loyalty program for Hilton hotels and resorts. It provides benefits and earnings on eligible stays at 27 Hilton brands, from full-service luxury brands like Waldorf Astoria and Conrad to select-service brands like Hilton Garden Inn and Hampton by Hilton. Hilton also launched its Select by Hilton collection earlier this year, adding Yotel as the collection's first brand. The Hilton Honors program offers various ways to earn and redeem Hilton points, too, including many options beyond hotel stays. One of these options is Hilton Honors Adventures, which lets you earn and redeem points for adventure-driven travel experiences. Initial partners for Hilton Honors Adventures are AutoCamp and Explora Journeys. When you book directly with Hilton, you'll earn points and benefits based on your membership tier. For the rest of this article, I'll assume you book through Hilton (not an online travel agency or other method) when discussing benefits and earnings. Related: The 22 best Hilton hotels in the world Hilton Honors membership tiers You'll progress up the Hilton Honors membership tiers as you stay at Hilton properties each calendar year. Once you've earned a specific membership tier, you'll enjoy its benefits for the rest of the calendar year in which you earned it and for the entire next calendar year. You can also snag Hilton Honors elite status through a status match or as a cardmember of select American Express cards. Comparison of Hilton Honors membership tiers | Membership tier | Qualification requirements per calendar year | Key benefits | Which credit cards give automatic access to this membership tier? | |---|---|---|---| | Member | None | Discounted rates, waived resort fees on award stays and Wi-Fi access | None | | Silver | Stay four times, stay for 10 nights or spend $2,500 | A 20% bonus on base points earned through stays and the fifth-night-free benefit on standard reward stays | | | Gold | Stay 15 times, stay for 25 nights or spend $6,000 | An 80% bonus on base points earned through stays, a choice of a My Way on-property benefit on each stay and space-available room upgrades | | | Diamond | Stay 25 times, stay for 50 nights or spend $11,500 | A 100% bonus on base points earned through stays, executive lounge access and premium Wi-Fi access | | | Diamond Reserve | Stay 40 times or 80 nights and spend $18,000 | A 120% bonus on base points earned through stays, 4 p.m. guaranteed late checkout, premium club access and one confirmable upgrade reward | None | Check out the following sections to learn more about each of these Hilton Honors membership tiers and other benefits you can enjoy on Hilton Honors stays. Hilton Honors member Once you join the Hilton Honors program, you'll be a member. The primary benefits of being a Hilton Honors member are: - Access to book the Hilton Honors discount rate - Waived resort fees when you pay for your stay using solely points or a promotional free night reward - The ability to choose your room from available rooms up to 24 hours before check-in - Free Wi-Fi throughout the hotel - The ability to earn points on stays - Late checkout, upon request and subject to availability It's free to join the Hilton Honors program, so you might as well join now if you aren't already a member. Hilton Honors Silver You'll earn Hilton Honors Silver status after you stay four times, stay for 10 nights or spend $2,500 in a calendar year. Eligible spending includes room rates and charges billed to your room (such as spa, dining and other incidental charges) from bookings made directly with Hilton or approved channels. The primary benefits of Hilton Silver status include: - A 20% bonus on base points earned through stays - Two complimentary bottles of water per stay at select hotels - A fifth night free on standard reward stays of five consecutive nights or more (up to four free nights per stay and only when you book solely with points) - Access to a spa discount of 15% on a single treatment when staying at Hilton all-inclusive properties with a spa You'll also enjoy Hilton Silver status as a cardmember benefit of the Hilton Honors American Express Card. Unfortunately, Hilton Honors eliminated rollover nights beginning in 2026, although qualifying nights rolled over from 2025 can still count toward 2026 status. Hilton Honors Gold You'll earn Hilton Honors Gold status after you stay 15 times, stay for 25 nights or spend $6,000 in a calendar year. The primary benefits of Hilton Gold status include: - An 80% bonus on base points earned through stays - A choice of a My Way on-property benefit on each stay (which may include the option to select a daily food-and-beverage credit or continental breakfast) - Space-available room upgrades to preferred rooms (including up to executive floor room types) at select brands and properties You'll also get Hilton Gold status as a cardmember benefit of the Hilton Honors American Express Surpass Card, the Hilton Honors American Express Business Card, the American Express Platinum Card and the Business Platinum Card from American Express (enrollment may be required). You can also earn Gold status through the end of the next calendar year if you spend $20,000 on eligible purchases on the Hilton Honors American Express Card within a calendar year. Related: Which Hilton hotels offer free breakfast? A guide to brand and elite benefits Hilton Honors Diamond You'll earn Hilton Honors Diamond status after you stay 25 times, stay for 50 nights or spend $11,500 in a calendar year. The primary benefits of Hilton Diamond status include: - A 100% bonus on base points earned through stays - Executive lounge access when available - Premium Wi-Fi access during stays at select brands - Space-available room upgrades to preferred rooms (including up to junior, standard or one-bedroom suites) at select brands and properties You can also obtain Hilton Diamond status as a cardmember benefit of the Hilton Honors American Express Aspire Card. Cardmembers of the Hilton Honors American Express Surpass Card and The Hilton Honors American Express Business Card can also earn Diamond status through the end of the next calendar year if they spend $40,000 on eligible purchases on their card in a calendar year. You'll secure lifetime Hilton Diamond status once you've earned Hilton Diamond status for 10 years (the years don't need to be consecutive) and either stay 1,000 nights (paid and reward nights count) or spend $200,000 across your account's lifetime. Hilton Honors Diamond Reserve You'll earn Hilton Honors Diamond Reserve status after you stay 40 times or 80 nights and spend $18,000 in a calendar year. The primary benefits of Hilton Diamond Reserve status include: - A 120% bonus on base points earned through stays - 4 p.m. guaranteed late checkout - Premium club access, including access to the expanding collection of premium clubs - A confirmable upgrade reward, which lets you confirm a premium room upgrade (up to a suite) at the time of booking for a stay of up to seven nights Hilton status match and challenge Hilton Honors usually offers a status match and challenge to select elite members of other hotel loyalty programs. To request a Hilton Honors status match, you must submit proof of your status in another program via an online form. If Hilton approves your request, you'll get Hilton Gold status for 90 days. You can keep Gold status through March 31, 2028, if you stay for six nights during your 90-day trial period. Meanwhile, if you stay 12 nights within your 90-day trial period, Hilton will upgrade you to Diamond status through March 31, 2028. Related: Complete guide to airline status matches and challenges Milestone bonuses and status gifts Hilton offers its members several additional benefits based on the number of eligible nights they stay each calendar year. Once you stay 40 eligible nights in a calendar year, you'll get 10,000 bonus points. You'll then earn an additional 10,000 bonus points for every additional 10 eligible nights (up to 180) in a calendar year. Plus, you'll earn an additional 30,000 bonus points once you stay 60 eligible nights in a calendar year. And once you stay 120 eligible nights in a calendar year, you can choose a confirmable upgrade reward or 30,000 bonus points. If you stay 60 eligible nights in a calendar year, you can also gift Hilton Gold status to another member. And if you stay 100 eligible nights in a calendar year, you can gift Hilton Diamond status to another member. However, you can only gift status to one other member per year. Benefits for Hilton members at Small Luxury Hotels of the World properties You can book select Small Luxury Hotels of the World properties through Hilton Honors. Hilton Honors members get the following benefits when staying at participating SLH hotels: - Ability to earn Hilton points on stays (you can also redeem Hilton points for SLH stays) - Free Wi-Fi - Complimentary late checkout (subject to availability) Plus, Hilton Honors Gold members and above also enjoy: - Space-available room upgrades - Continental breakfast for you and up to one additional guest Related: The coolest SLH hotels you can book with Hilton Honors points Benefits for Hilton members on Explora Journeys You'll earn eligible nights, stays and spend toward Hilton Honors status on Explora Journeys. You'll also enjoy some extra perks based on your Hilton Honors tier as follows: - Member: 5% savings on all Journeys, a welcome gift and 5% savings on Journeys merchandise - Silver: Member benefits, plus a signature loyalty delight and dedicated customer support - Gold: Silver benefits, plus access to a cocktail event with ship leadership and a surprise gift or ritual - Diamond: Gold benefits, plus complimentary laundry service (one bag per Journey) and experience credits for destination experiences and ocean wellness - Diamond Reserve: Diamond benefits, plus complimentary laundry service (one bag per day), a behind-the-scenes bridge tour (upon availability) and a private transfer to the port How to earn Hilton points As you interact with the Hilton Honors program, you'll find many ways to earn points. For a detailed discussion, I highly recommend checking out our guide on earning Hilton points, but here's an overview of your options. Hotel stays One of the easiest ways to earn Hilton points is through hotel stays. On eligible stays, you'll usually earn as follows on charges to your folio from up to four rooms: - 3 points per dollar spent, plus 3,000 bonus points per 10 nights completed within the same stay, at LivSmart Studios properties - 5 points per dollar spent at Home2 Suites outside China, Homewood Suites, Spark, Tru, Yotel and Apartment Collection properties - 10 points per dollar spent at Home2 Suites in China and other Hilton brands Of course, as I mentioned above, you'll earn additional bonus points on stays if you have Hilton elite status. Plus, you may earn bonus points through current Hilton promotions. Related: 8 best Hilton all-inclusive resorts Hilton credit cards Hilton Amex cards are also a great way to earn points. Here's a look at the earning rates, welcome offers and annual fees on some of our favorite Hilton credit cards. | Card | Welcome offer | Earning rates | Annual fee | |---|---|---|---| | | Earn 200,000 bonus points after spending $6,000 on purchases in the first six months of card membership. | | | | | Earn 130,000 bonus points and a free night reward after spending $3,000 on purchases in the first six months of card membership. | | | | | Earn 150,000 bonus points and a free night reward after spending $8,000 on purchases in the first six months of card membership. | | | | | Earn 70,000 bonus points and a free night reward after spending $2,000 on purchases in the first six months of card membership. | | | I have the Hilton Aspire Card and find it offers far more value than its annual fee since I maximize its benefits. Plus, earning 14 points per dollar spent on purchases at Hilton properties is unbeatable. But if you don't maximize the annual free night reward and don't fully use the up to $400 Hilton resort statement credit (up to $200 statement credits biannually) each year, the Hilton Aspire may not be the right card for you. Related: Hilton Surpass vs. Hilton Aspire: Do you want Gold or Diamond status? Transfer rewards to Hilton You can also earn points by transferring rewards to Hilton Honors. Specifically, you can transfer American Express Membership Rewards points to Hilton Honors at a 1:2 ratio, meaning 1,000 Amex points could become 2,000 Hilton points. You can also transfer Bilt Points to Hilton Honors at a 1:1 ratio. You can usually get more value by transferring these points to other loyalty programs, so I wouldn't transfer my Amex or Bilt points to Hilton Honors. But even if you plan to transfer Amex or Bilt points to Hilton, it's usually a good idea to wait until you're ready to book your stay. Related: How (and why) you should earn transferable credit card points Hilton partners You can earn Hilton points when shopping or interacting with several partners. For example, you can earn points on eligible Alamo, Enterprise and National car rentals. You can also earn extra points at participating restaurants through the Hilton Honors Dining program and opt in to earn Hilton points on Lyft rides. Plus, you can earn Hilton points with Hilton's Vacation Ownership brand and on Explora Journeys. Hilton Honors event planner program Hilton Honors members can earn 2 points per dollar spent on guest rooms, meeting rooms and more (on up to $100,000 spent) through the Hilton Honors event planner program when holding a qualifying event at a participating Hilton property. Buy Hilton points Finally, you can buy Hilton points to boost your account balance. TPG's September 2026 valuations peg the value of Hilton points at 0.4 cents per point, and during the best sales, you can buy Hilton points for 0.5 cents each. So, you'll usually only want to buy Hilton points when doing so lets you book a high-value redemption. How to redeem Hilton points Just as there are many ways to earn Hilton points, there are plenty of ways to redeem your points. Check out our guide on redeeming Hilton points for all the details, but here's an overview of the best and worst ways to redeem Hilton points. Free night awards Hilton Honors doesn't publish an award chart and instead uses dynamic award pricing. However, there appears to be an unpublished cap on award pricing for each property, and standard award nights currently top out at 250,000 points at the most luxurious properties. If you want a good deal, consider using the Points Explorer tool to see point ranges at various properties over the next 30 days. Likewise, you can view monthly award pricing for a specific property by selecting "Shop by price" instead of stay dates. To get the best value when redeeming Hilton points, book an award stay for a standard room for five, 10, 15 or 20 nights. Assuming you have Hilton Silver status or higher, you'll get every fifth night free when redeeming points for stays of five nights or longer. Check TPG's current valuations and try to get at least our valuation of Hilton points on your redemption. Although you can redeem Hilton points for premium rooms, doing so will usually not provide good value. Related: 6 ways to maximize Hilton Honors redemptions Points & Money rewards You might want to book a Points & Money reward if you run short on points. This booking method lets you redeem any combination of points and cash for a stay. For example, here's one option for a stay that would otherwise cost 87,000 points or $367.13. You'll earn points on the money portion of Points & Money rewards stays at participating hotels. Pool or transfer Hilton points Hilton Honors is generous in allowing its members to pool and transfer points at no cost. You can pool or transfer points in increments of 1,000 points, up to 500,000. Each Hilton Honors member can send up to 500,000 points and receive up to 2 million points via combined pooling and transfer transactions each calendar year. However, each member can only make up to six transfers to other accounts and up to six points pooling transactions each calendar year. New Hilton Honors members can only pool, transfer or receive points 30 or more days after enrollment if they have account activity. Otherwise, they must wait at least 90 days after enrollment before pooling, transferring or receiving points without account activity. Hilton Honors Experiences Redeeming points for Hilton Honors Experiences has offered me strong value in the past. As such, I periodically check whether any experiences at my upcoming destinations are appealing. Be sure to check the paid rates, when available, before booking to determine whether redeeming points for the experience will provide good value. Related: How Hilton Honors points unlocked a premium NCAA basketball experience in Chicago Hilton Honors redemptions to avoid There are a few specific types of Hilton Honors redemptions that you'll want to avoid, as they offer extremely low value for your points. As you read through this section, keep in mind that TPG's September 2026 valuations pegged the value of Hilton points at 0.4 cents each. - Amazon Shop with Points: You can redeem 700 Hilton Honors points for a dollar of value at Amazon checkout, meaning you'll only get 0.14 cents per point. - Lyft credits: You can redeem 4,500 Hilton Honors points for a $10 Lyft credit, meaning you'd only get 0.22 cents per point. - Car rentals: A sample two-day Alamo car rental I priced out would cost $257.55 or 96,159 Hilton Honors points, meaning you'd only get 0.27 cents per point. - Transferring to airline miles: The transfer ratios usually make this a poor option unless you have no other use for Hilton points. I'd also add most premium-room reward nights to this list, as they usually offer a much lower cents-per-point redemption rate than standard-room rewards. Is Hilton Honors worth it? Hilton Honors is a popular program for a reason. Its main positives include the following: - Easy-to-earn status via credit cards - High earning rates on both card spending and hotel stays - A wide range of brands, including luxury, budget and extended stay - Large global footprint However, I personally find it difficult to get outsize value from Hilton Honors points. Hence, it isn't one of my primary hotel loyalty programs. Its negatives include: - Getting good value when redeeming Hilton points can be difficult. - Many elite benefits, even at higher tiers, are subject to availability and vary significantly by property. - Premium room reward pricing doesn't scale well, making it a poor redemption option in most cases. Despite these drawbacks, Hilton Honors can still be a very rewarding program, particularly if you can get elite status through a credit card and regularly stay at Hilton properties. Even if you don't stay with Hilton frequently, it's worth enrolling before your next stay to earn points and enjoy member benefits. For rates and fees of the Hilton Honors Amex, click here. For rates and fees of the Hilton Amex Aspire, click here. For rates and fees of the Hilton Surpass, click here. For rates and fees of the Hilton Business Amex, click here. Frequently asked questions Hilton Honors is Hilton's free hotel loyalty program. Once you join the program, you'll earn points on eligible stays at more than 9,000 properties worldwide that participate in Hilton Honors. Plus, you'll be able to redeem Hilton points for free nights and experiences. The program also offers elite status tiers that provide perks like bonus points and room upgrades. The fastest ways to earn Hilton Honors points are through hotel stays, Hilton cobranded credit cards and limited-time bonus point promotions. However, perhaps the quickest way to earn Hilton points is to simply purchase them. Hilton Honors elite status can provide meaningful value, especially for frequent travelers. Benefits may include bonus points on stays, complimentary breakfast or food-and-beverage credits at select brands, room upgrades and executive lounge access. However, benefits can vary widely by property, so the value of elite status depends heavily on how often and where you stay. You can earn Hilton Honors elite status by staying a required number of nights, completing a specific number of stays or meeting annual spending thresholds with Hilton. Hilton also offers shortcuts to elite status through select cobranded credit cards and status match opportunities for elite members of other hotel loyalty programs. Hilton Honors points are usually only worth buying during a promotion and when you have a specific redemption in mind. Since Hilton uses dynamic award pricing, buying points can occasionally help you book an expensive hotel stay for less than the cash rate. Yes. Hilton Honors points expire after 24 months of account inactivity. You must complete at least one stay at a Hilton property, earn points with a Hilton credit card, earn or redeem points with a Hilton partner, buy or donate points, or register for a Hilton promotion within 24 months to keep your Hilton Honors account active. Hilton Honors members with Silver status or higher receive every fifth night free on standard room reward stays booked entirely with points. The benefit applies automatically to eligible stays of five nights or longer, and you can get up to four free nights per reservation.

item.title: Chase Freedom Q4 categories: Up to 7% back on dining, grocery stores and American Red Cross donations
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy Score: 4.84
Chase Freedom Q4 categories: Up to 7% back on dining, grocery stores and American Red Cross donations Editor's Note If you have the Chase Freedom Flex® (see rates and fees) or legacy Chase Freedom®* in your wallet, the three rotating categories for Q4 have been announced. From Oct. 1 through Dec. 31, you'll earn up to 7% cash back (or up to 7 points per dollar spent) on dining, grocery stores and American Red Cross donations. You must activate your categories by Dec. 14 to earn at these rates (on up to $1,500 in combined spending across these categories; then 1% back or 1 point per dollar spent). Here's what you need to know about this quarter's categories. Last chance: Activate your Chase Freedom fourth-quarter categories *This card is no longer available to new applicants. The information for the Chase Freedom has been collected independently by The Points Guy. The card details on this page have not been reviewed or provided by the card issuer. Chase Freedom Q4 2026 categories From Oct. 1 through Dec. 31, Freedom and Freedom Flex cardholders will earn 5% cash back (or 5 points per dollar spent) across these bonus categories (on up to $1,500 in combined purchases; then 1% back or 1 point per dollar spent): - Dining (Freedom Flex cardholders will earn an elevated 7% cash back on these purchases for Q4) - Grocery stores - American Red Cross donations Dining already appeared as a bonus category earlier this year, so those who dine out often or order a lot of food delivery will appreciate a second chance to earn up to 7% cash back. Grocery stores are one of the most common quarterly bonus categories on the Freedom cards, while this is the first time we're seeing American Red Cross donations as a standalone category. And extra good news for Freedom Flex cardholders: the card will stop charging foreign transaction fees from Sept. 20, making it an excellent choice for dining and grocery purchases both in the U.S. and abroad in Q4. (We're unsure if legacy Freedom cardholders will enjoy the same privilege; check your Freedom card benefits guide in your online account after Sept. 20.) Activate this quarter's categories now to unlock their bonus-earning potential. You must activate by Dec. 14, but keep in mind that these categories will not go live until Oct. 1. It's simple to complete this process through your Chase account; just provide your last name, the last four digits of your card and your ZIP code. Analyzing the Q4 bonus categories The fourth quarter is a time when many people rack up plenty of charges from restaurants and grocery stores, between the holidays, end-of-year travel and gatherings with loved ones. Since dining and groceries are likely two of the highest spending categories for many Freedom cardholders, it's nice to see them offered as bonus categories at the same time. If you're feeling in a charitable mood this holiday season, consider using your eligible Freedom card to donate to the American Red Cross. Here are the details: - Dining: If you're a Freedom Flex cardholder, Chase has confirmed that you'll be eligible for a boosted 7% cash back on dining purchases, including eligible takeout and delivery; legacy Freedom cardholders (no longer open to applicants) will earn 5% cash back. 7% cash back is among the highest rates available for dining purchases, so Freedom Flex cardholders should make a point to charge those purchases — both in the U.S. and internationally — to that card in Q4. - Grocery stores: Whether you're buying weekly groceries, preparing for winter storms or gearing up for holiday meals, you'll be able to get 5% cash back on your grocery purchases with your eligible Freedom card. (Note that Walmart, Target, wholesale clubs, discount stores and some drugstores are not eligible for the quarterly bonus.) - American Red Cross donations: If you decide to donate to the American Red Cross in Q4, you'll earn 5% cash back on your donation. While some cards offer bonus rewards on charitable donations, it isn't too common. That makes your eligible Freedom card a great pick for any donations to this particular charity. Make sure to make your donation directly through the Red Cross, otherwise your purchase may not code correctly for the 5% bonus cash back. Remember that Chase limits the 5% cash back (or 5 points per dollar spent) you can earn to the first $1,500 spent in combined bonus categories each quarter. After you reach the maximum, you'll earn 1% back (or 1 point per dollar spent) on these purchases.
