and Starbucks | Chase Freedom bonus categories FAQs How do rotating categories work? Each quarter, Chase announces a set of bonus categories that earn 5% cash back (or 5 points per dollar) for the next three months (on up to $1,500 in combined spending). Generally, these categories are announced halfway through the month before the new quarter starts, giving cardholders time to activate new categories. However, you can activate your categories until midway through the last month of the quarter. The categories tend to repeat periodically. For instance, grocery stores, restaurants and gas stations are all common categories you'll notice frequently pop up on the bonus calendar. So, depending on the categories and whether you can maximize them, these two cards can offer quite a nice chunk of cash back or bonus points over the year. How much cash back can I earn each quarter? Chase limits the 5% cash back (or 5 points per dollar) to the first $1,500 spent in combined bonus categories each quarter you activate the bonus. While that may not sound like a lot, that cash back adds up over time. Maximizing the cash-back categories each quarter, you'll earn $75 in cash back quarterly and up to $300 per year. For a no-annual-fee credit card, that's a lot of value. Alternatively, suppose you have a card that earns transferable Chase Ultimate Rewards points, like the Chase Sapphire Preferred® Card (see rates and fees). In that case, you can combine the rewards from your Chase Freedom or Freedom Flex card with those you earn from your more premium Ultimate Rewards-earning card. By doing this, your rewards become fully transferable. If you combine rewards this way, your $300 in bonus cash back would be worth 30,000 Ultimate Rewards points. TPG's September 2026 valuations peg Chase points at 2.05 cents apiece, making the 30,000 points you can earn in a year worth $615. How do I activate my 5% categories each quarter? You can head to Chase's site to activate your 5% cash back (or 5 points per dollar) categories for this quarter. You can also register through the Chase mobile app. Here's how to register: - Head to the Chase bonus activation page, or log in to your Chase account. - Enter your last name, the last four digits of your card number and your billing ZIP code. If you don't have your card on hand, log in to your Chase account to retrieve these digits. - Click "Activate your 5%" to register. - If you have multiple Chase Freedom cards, make sure to register each one. - Save a screenshot of your activation in case of any issues later, though you should also receive a "You're Activated!" confirmation email. Can I have both the Chase Freedom and the Chase Freedom Flex to double my earning potential? Yes, you can have both cards. So, if you already have the Chase Freedom and want to add the Chase Freedom Flex to your wallet, you're free to do so. Remember that the original Freedom card is no longer open to new applicants. If you'd rather only have one, though, the Freedom Flex is available as a product change. Of course, you'll also want to ensure you're eligible for a new Chase card. How do I maximize my Freedom and Freedom Flex cards? The most important thing is to activate your card to earn 5% cash back (or 5 points per dollar) each quarter in the specific categories and then use it for purchases in those categories. You can set up a recurring reminder in your calendar or sign up for the TPG newsletter. (We send out a reminder when it's time to activate every quarter, plus tips and tricks for how to maximize your card strategy and score some excellent award redemptions.) In addition to the rotating bonus categories, the Freedom Flex accrues 5% cash back on all other travel booked through Chase Travel, 3% cash back on drugstore purchases, 3% cash back on dining (including eligible delivery services) and 1% unlimited cash back on all other purchases. Better yet, when paired with a Chase credit card that earns fully transferable Ultimate Rewards points, such as the Chase Sapphire Reserve® (see rates and fees) or the Chase Sapphire Preferred, the Chase Freedom Flex's 5% cash back effectively becomes 5 Ultimate Rewards points per dollar. You can learn all about this in our guide detailing the Chase Trifecta. Bottom line If you're a Chase Freedom or Freedom Flex cardholder, your Q4 categories include dining, grocery stores and American Red Cross donations. Most of these purchases will earn 5% cash back (or 5 points per dollar spent) from October through December. The exception is dining purchases on the Freedom Flex, which will earn an elevated 7% cash back (or 7 points per dollar spent). Activate these categories now so you don't miss out on any bonus rewards when these categories go live. And remember that Chase limits your quarterly bonus category earnings to the first $1,500 of combined spending each quarter. To learn more, read our full review of the Chase Freedom Flex. Apply here: Chase Freedom Flex TPG featured card | 4X | Earn 4X Membership Rewards® points per dollar spent on purchases at restaurants worldwide, on up to $50,000 in purchases per calendar year, then 1X points for the rest of the year. | | 4X | Earn 4X Membership Rewards® points per dollar spent at US supermarkets, on up to $25,000 in purchases per calendar year, then 1X points for the rest of the year. | | 5X | Earn 5X Membership Rewards® points on prepaid hotel stays booked through AmexTravel.com or the Amex Travel App™. | | 3X | Earn 3X Membership Rewards® points on flights booked through AmexTravel.com, the Amex Travel App™, or purchased directly from airlines. | | 2X | Earn 2X Membership Rewards® points on prepaid car rentals booked through AmexTravel.com or the Amex Travel App™ and cruises booked and paid through AmexTravel.com. | | 1X | Earn 1X Membership Rewards® point per dollar spent on all other eligible purchases. |

item.title: Earn a first-year dollar-for-dollar cash-back match with these Discover offers
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy Score: 4.77
Earn a first-year dollar-for-dollar cash-back match with these Discover offers While they may not get as much fanfare as cards from giants like American Express and Chase, Discover cards are great choices for cash-back enthusiasts, beginner credit card users and simplicity-lovers alike. As Discover's cards migrate to Capital One's network, they're attracting fresh attention. If you've decided now is the right time to apply for a Discover card, make sure you know what offer you're getting. Discover doesn't typically change the welcome offers on its cards, so the answer to "When should I apply?" depends more on your personal situation than on the specific card's offer. Discover it Cash Back Best for: Those looking for flexible spending categories Current welcome offer: Receive an unlimited dollar-for-dollar cash-back match for your first cardholder year (no spending requirement). This is the standard offer for this card, so now is a good time to apply. Annual fee: $0 Key benefits: - 5% cash back in rotating quarterly categories (on up to $1,500 in combined spending each quarter; activation required) - 5% cash back on hotels, car rentals and attractions booked through Capital One Travel - 5% cash back on Capital One Entertainment purchases - 1% cash back on all other purchases - Access to Capital One Offers - Fraud protection and free credit score access To learn more, check out our full review of the Discover it® Cash Back. Apply here: Discover it® Cash Back Discover it Student Cash Back Best for: Students who want the highest welcome offer available from Discover Current welcome offer: Earn a $100 statement credit after spending $300 on purchases in the first three months from account opening. Plus, receive an unlimited dollar-for-dollar cash-back match for your first cardholder year (no spending requirement). Since this welcome offer lets you earn more than the standard first-year cash-back match, it's a great one to go for if you qualify. The statement credit portion of this offer is a limited-time offer, so don't wait to apply. Annual fee: $0 Key benefits: - 5% cash back in rotating quarterly categories (on up to $1,500 in combined spending each quarter; activation required) - 5% cash back on hotels, car rentals and attractions booked through Capital One Travel - 5% cash back on Capital One Entertainment purchases - 1% cash back on all other purchases - Access to Capital One Offers - No credit score required to apply - Fraud protection and free credit score access To learn more, check out our full review of the Discover it® Student Cash Back. Apply here: Discover it® Student Cash Back Discover it Miles Best for: Those who want to earn solid rewards on everyday purchases Current welcome offer: Receive an unlimited match on all miles you earn in your first cardholder year (no spending requirement). This is the same offer we've seen on this card for a long time, so we don't recommend waiting for a different one. Annual fee: $0 Key benefits: - 5 miles per dollar spent on hotels, car rentals and attractions booked through Capital One Travel - 5 miles per dollar spent on Capital One Entertainment purchases - 1.5 miles per dollar spent on all other purchases - Access to Capital One Offers - Fraud protection and free credit score access To learn more, check out our full review of the Discover it® Miles . Apply here: Discover it® Miles Discover it Chrome Best for: Those who spend a moderate amount on gas and dining and don't have another card that earns bonus rewards on these categories Current welcome offer: Receive an unlimited dollar-for-dollar cash-back match for your first cardholder year (no spending requirement). We don't expect this offer to change any time soon, so we recommend applying now. Annual fee: $0 Key benefits: - 5% cash back on hotels, car rentals and attractions booked through Capital One Travel - 5% cash back on Capital One Entertainment purchases - 2% cash back on gas stations and restaurants (on up to $1,000 in combined spending each quarter) - 1% cash back on all other purchases - Access to Capital One Offers - Fraud protection and free credit score access To learn more, check out our full review of the Discover it® Chrome. Apply here: Discover it® Chrome Discover it Student Chrome Best for: Students who spend a lot on gas and dining Current welcome offer: Receive an unlimited dollar-for-dollar cash-back match for your first cardholder year (no spending requirement). We don't expect this offer to change any time soon, so now is a great time to apply. Annual fee: $0 Key benefits: - 5% cash back on hotels, car rentals and attractions booked through Capital One Travel - 5% cash back on Capital One Entertainment purchases - 2% cash back on gas stations and restaurants (on up to $1,000 in combined spending each quarter) - 1% cash back on all other purchases - Access to Capital One Offers - Fraud protection and free credit score access Apply here: Discover it® Student Chrome Which Discover card is right for you? Discover's cards are geared toward cash-back fans and anyone looking to build or repair credit. While you won't find comprehensive travel benefits or merchant statement credits on any of their cards, that may be a welcome sight for some. Since all of Discover's cards have very similar perks, your choice will come down to which card's earning rates you prefer. If you're a student, you'll likely be best off with one of the issuer's student cards, since those should be the easiest to get approved for among the cards mentioned here. Who is eligible for a Discover card? As with any credit card, Discover may consider several factors when deciding whether to approve your application. These may include your credit score and previous history with the issuer. It's worth noting that Discover doesn't require a credit score for its two student cards, making either a great choice for those who are eligible. You'll need to be a student enrolled at least part-time at a college or university and be at least 18 years old to qualify. For any of its credit cards, Discover will require some form of income to get approved. If you're applying for one of its standard credit cards, expect a full-time job to be the requirement for approval. If you're applying for a student card, Discover states that a part-time job may qualify. If you're a student and you don't have a job right now, consider asking a family member to add you as an authorized user on their card. Otherwise, you'll need to wait until you have income to get your own credit card. Significant savings could also qualify you for a credit card, but keep in mind that you'll need a balance in the tens of thousands to make this a workable alternative. Bottom line If you're looking for a simple cash-back card to add to your wallet or you need a solid option for building credit, it's worth considering a Discover card. Since all Discover cards have no annual fee, they're easy to justify keeping over the long term. With all Discover products migrating over to Capital One's network, any Discover card you apply for now will be on Capital One's network. That means you'll enjoy additional benefits on your card, including access to Capital One Travel and Capital One Entertainment, as well as boosted earnings on these purchases through these two portals.

item.title: Delta ends 19-year Monterey hiatus, returns to Central Coast with 2 routes
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy Score: 4.52
Delta ends 19-year Monterey hiatus, returns to Central Coast with 2 routes Delta Air Lines is returning to California's Central Coast for the first time in almost 19 years. In December, the airline will launch service from the Golden State's Monterey Regional Airport (MRY). It's a return that's certainly a long time coming. Delta last operated regular service to the airport in January 2008. Now, most of its top competitors — including American Airlines, United Airlines and Alaska Airlines — have flights from the airport. Delta's latest go-around in Monterey is set to begin on Dec. 19, right as the holiday season kicks off. Delta's 2 routes from Monterey The carrier plans to offer nonstop flights to two of its western hubs: - Twice-daily service to Los Angeles International Airport (LAX) - Daily service to Salt Lake City International Airport (SLC) Both routes will be served by Embraer 175 Delta Connection regional jets. Sardines, Steinbeck and sea otters: TPG's guide to exploring Monterey, California Monterey Regional Airport: What to know MRY is a tiny airport just miles from the California coast that gives travelers easier access to destinations like Monterey County, Carmel and Big Sur, not to mention the scenic Highway 1, along the state's rugged Pacific coastline. If you can find a fare that fits your budget, flying directly to Monterey is a great way to reach the area without a long drive or risking traffic. In comparison, Monterey is about two hours from the region's largest hub at San Francisco International Airport (SFO). Meanwhile, the drive from MRY to San Jose Mineta International Airport (SJC) takes about an hour and a half. Monterey's airport only has a small handful of gates, and the terminal can certainly get busy when you get a couple of flights departing around the same time. So I'm curious to see how the airport fares when another major carrier joins the mix. However, adding one of the nation's three biggest airlines — and service to two major hubs — will certainly be good news for travelers in the region. Tip: If you're flying from MRY, I'd suggest getting to the airport a little early. There's a local restaurant outside security, and you can grab a bite to eat and do some sightseeing (or planespotting) on the large observation deck. Read more: What makes a good destination for a company retreat — and why TPG chose Monterey How the competition stacks up Delta will have competition on one of its routes, as United already offers flights between MRY and LAX. With these two routes, Delta will serve all but one of its western hubs. Left out of this route announcement is Seattle-Tacoma International Airport (SEA), which already has MRY service on Alaska Airlines, Delta's top Pacific Northwest rival. Related reading:

item.title: American's next premium plans: Way more Flagship Suites, new (and improved) lounges
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy Score: 4.43
American's next premium plans: Way more Flagship Suites, new (and improved) lounges It's about to get a lot easier to book a flight featuring one of American Airlines' fancy new Flagship Suites. With brand-new planes coming and older ones getting makeovers, the the posh new business-class product will be on many more aircraft in the coming months — and years. American debuted its next-generation suites last year to plenty of fanfare. It was the airline's first premium seat with sliding privacy doors. But until now, you had to be pretty savvy to actually score a flight featuring the new suites. As of today, AA's Flagship seats are only available on a small portion of its fleet: - A handful of brand-new Boeing 787-9 Dreamliners - A few long-range, single-aisle Airbus A321XLRs - Plus, one Boeing 777-300ER that just got a total on-board makeover with the new seats. But there are a lot more planes still to come. Older planes to get new cabin (and suites) American has announced its new flagship cabin will get installed on nearly its entire long-haul fleet over the next few years. In fact, as it stands today there's only one type of twin-aisle jet American hasn't slated for a refresh: its Boeing 787-9 Dreamliners that got delivered prior to 2025. It begs the question: Could those jets also get Flagship Suites eventually? "It's an active debate," Rhonda Crawford, American's senior vice president of customer experience and design, told me earlier this month, adding: "I would just say everything's on the table right now." American essentially has two types of 787-9s flying today. The newest planes seat 244 passengers and include the premium-heavy layout that features 51 of the Flagship Suites that debuted last year. The airline also has a 285-seat legacy configuration that dates back as far as the mid-2010s. It's worth watching how AA handles its Dreamliner fleet in the coming years. Regardless, international flying on American will certainly look a lot different by the end of this decade with a refresh to nearly all the planes it uses for long-haul service. Narrowbody planes set for upgrade, too By the way: American's single-aisle planes are slated for a big makeover, too. Last month, the carrier announced it would bring back seatback screens and outfit those jets with more first-class and extra legroom seats. That rollout is set to begin in 2028. 'First quarter' of a lounge glow-up Meanwhile, American has also been busy making major announcements about its plans on the ground. After promising a "steady stream" of airport lounge news late last year, the carrier has followed through. American has revealed new or significantly expanded clubs in Austin, Charlotte, Chicago, Dallas, Nashville, New York and Washington. On top of that, the airline has been upgrading the food it serves in its outposts. Apparently, American isn't done yet. "We are in the beginning quarter," Crawford said of the carrier's lounge plans. "There's more to come, and there's more in the pipeline, for sure," she added. "Lots of opportunity for refurbs and rebuilds, and expansions, and restorations, and all of the above." Provisions plans I wouldn't be surprised if you saw more of AA's newest lounge concept called Provisions by Admirals Club. That's the new permanent grab-and-go lounge setup the airline debuted last summer at Charlotte Douglas International Airport (CLT). Since then, American has announced additional Provisions locations for John F. Kennedy International Airport (JFK) and Dallas Fort Worth International Airport (DFW). American's inaugural CLT Provisions location was more functional in nature. But it appears the carrier has more elaborate planes for its JFK and DFW locations — including a full-service coffee bar in New York. "You'll see us continue to optimize and hone in [on] those and improve those," Crawford said. Grab-and-go lounge locations can be a helpful way for airlines to reduce crowding in their main clubs. Those outposts allow members who only need a cup of coffee and a quick bite to eat to briefly stop in, grab what they need, and leave without occupying seats. Related reading:

item.title: Citi / AAdvantage Executive statement credits: What they are and how to use them
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy Score: 4.18
Citi / AAdvantage Executive statement credits: What they are and how to use them Editor's Note The Citi® / AAdvantage® Executive World Legend Mastercard® (see rates and fees) is American Airlines' premium cobranded credit card with Citi, best known for its complimentary Admirals Club membership. Following a recent refresh, the card also offers a collection of statement credits that can help offset its $695 annual fee. These include credits for American Airlines Vacations, inflight and Admirals Club purchases, Avis and Budget rentals and Global Entry or TSA PreCheck application fees. Here's a closer look at each of the Citi / AAdvantage Executive's statement credits and how to use them. Overview of Citi / AAdvantage Executive credits The Citi / AA Executive Mastercard offers five statement credits covering expenses ranging from American Airlines travel and inflight purchases to rental cars and ride-hailing services. | Credit | Value | |---|---| | American Airlines Vacation Credit | Up to $500 annually; split into two periods (January to June and July to December) | | Inflight and Admirals Club purchases | Up to $100 per calendar year | | Avis/Budget | Up to $120 per calendar year | | Global Entry/TSA PreCheck | Up to $120 every four years | | Lyft | Up to $180 annually; $15 per month (after taking three eligible rides in a calendar month) | Related: Is the Citi / AAdvantage Executive World Legend Mastercard worth it? American Airlines Vacations credit The Citi / AA Executive Mastercard offers up to $500 in American Airlines Vacations statement credits each calendar year. The benefit is split into two six-month periods: up to $250 from Jan. 1 through June 30, and another up to $250 from July 1 through Dec. 31. To qualify, you'll need to book an eligible American Airlines Vacations travel package or experience through AAVacations.com and pay with your Citi / AA Executive card. This isn't a general American Airlines travel credit, so standalone airfare booked through AA.com won't qualify. If you can naturally use the full $500 annual benefit, it can offset a substantial portion of the card's $695 annual fee. But the value you actually get from this credit also depends on how American Airlines Vacations package pricing compares with booking your trip separately. When I priced a three-night trip for two from Dallas to Las Vegas, an American Airlines Vacations package with roundtrip American Airlines flights and a stay at the Bellagio cost $2,473. Booking the same flights directly with American cost $1,086, while booking the same room directly with the Bellagio cost $1,595, for a total of $2,681. In this case, the vacation package was already $208 cheaper than booking the components separately. After factoring in the card's $250 statement credit, the effective package cost dropped to $2,223 — a savings of $458 compared with booking separately. Package pricing can vary, though, so I'd still compare the cost of booking through American Airlines Vacations with booking each component separately before using the credit. Inflight and Admirals Club purchase credit The Citi / AA Executive Mastercard offers up to $100 in statement credits each calendar year on eligible American Airlines inflight and Admirals Club purchases. Eligible purchases can include food and beverages purchased onboard American Airlines flights, as well as eligible purchases at Admirals Club locations. While Admirals Clubs offer complimentary food and select drinks, you may encounter additional charges for premium beverages, such as cocktails or higher-end wines. For cardholders who regularly fly American, this is the card's easiest statement credit to use. Eligible purchases charged to your card will receive statement credits until you've reached the $100 annual maximum, so you don't have to keep track of a monthly or quarterly allotment. (It's also worth noting that some existing cardholders can temporarily stack this credit with the card's outgoing 25% discount on eligible inflight food and beverage purchases. Cardholders who applied before Aug. 23, 2026, will retain that benefit through Sept. 30, 2026; new cardholders don't receive the 25% discount.) Related: The Citi / AAdvantage Executive's new benefits are live: 6 things to do now Avis and Budget prepaid rental credit Citi / AA Executive cardholders can receive up to $120 in statement credits each calendar year on eligible prepaid Avis and Budget car rentals booked directly through Avis.com or Budget.com. This benefit can be useful if you rent cars at least occasionally, since a single rental could potentially use up much or all of the annual credit. However, you'll need to actively keep track of the requirements: The rental must be prepaid and booked directly with Avis or Budget to qualify, so bookings through third-party sites, travel agencies or other channels — including AA.com/cars — won't trigger the credit. This narrow eligibility window is where some cardholders run into trouble. The prepaid booking requirement itself carries an additional limitation: a $50 cancellation penalty if you cancel more than 24 hours before pickup or $150 if you cancel within 24 hours. If your travel plans are uncertain, those fees could easily erode the value of a $120 credit. I'd also compare prepaid Avis and Budget rates with other available rental options rather than booking with either company solely to use the credit. Saving $120 isn't particularly valuable if you're paying substantially more for the rental in the first place, especially given the risk of prepaid cancellation. Primary cardholders can also enroll for complimentary Avis President's Club status (through Aug. 31, 2028). The status includes perks such as upgrades (where available) and guaranteed availability up to a full-size car (with a confirmed reservation at least 24 hours in advance). These benefits — combined with the prepaid rental credit — can offset the inconvenience of booking directly, particularly for cardholders who rent regularly. Global Entry/TSA PreCheck credit The Citi / AA Executive Mastercard provides up to $120 in statement credits every four years toward a Global Entry or TSA PreCheck application fee. Eligible application fees charged to the card will receive a statement credit of up to $120. If you're choosing between the two programs, Global Entry is the better option for international travelers because it includes TSA PreCheck. If you already have a membership, you can use the credit to cover an eligible application fee for a friend or family member instead. Related: The best credit cards for Global Entry and TSA PreCheck Lyft credit The Citi / AA Executive Mastercard offers up to $180 in Lyft credits annually, but maximizing this benefit requires quite a lot of effort. You must complete three eligible Lyft rides in a calendar month before receiving $15 in credits for that month, and you'll need to meet that requirement every month to receive the full annual value. That makes this credit most useful for regular, committed Lyft users who already take at least three rides each month. If your Lyft use is more sporadic, I wouldn't place much value on this benefit, since taking extra rides solely to unlock a $15 credit is unlikely to make financial sense. If you can use the benefit naturally, make sure your Citi / AAdvantage Executive is linked to your account and keep the three-ride threshold in mind each month. Grubhub credit (only available to some existing cardholders) An up to $10 monthly credit for eligible Grubhub purchases is being phased out. Cardholders who applied for their Executive card before Aug. 23, 2026, receive the credit through Aug. 31, 2027; new cardholders don't. Bottom line The Citi / AAdvantage Executive offers a suite of statement credits that are best suited to American Airlines loyalists who can take advantage of the card's travel-focused benefits. The inflight and Global Entry credits are the easiest to use, while the AA Vacations and car rental credits require you to do some research. The Lyft credit is the hardest to get value from. You shouldn't value these credits at face value unless they fit your existing spending, but frequent AA flyers who can use several of them naturally may offset a meaningful portion of the card's $695 annual fee. To learn more, read our full review of the Citi / AAdvantage Executive. Apply here: Citi / AAdvantage Executive World Legend Mastercard

item.title: Air France to open one of New York JFK's biggest lounges at new Terminal One
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy Score: 3.95
Air France to open one of New York JFK's biggest lounges at new Terminal One New York's newest airport terminal is months away from opening at John F. Kennedy International Airport (JFK). And we just learned who scored the biggest lounge space. Air France plans to open a sprawling, 29,000 square foot club at JFK's new Terminal One, the airline announced Tuesday. It will be the French flag carrier's biggest lounge outside of Paris — and roughly triple the size of its current outpost in the airport's existing Terminal 1. Air France's new JFK lounge The new Air France Lounge will be one of the largest in any terminal at JFK — though the massive Delta One Lounge in Terminal 4 still reigns supreme at the airport. A sneak peek rendering of the club shared with TPG Tuesday shows a white and navy blue color palette that's been a staple in the newest lounges that Air France has opened (or renovated) in recent years. The facility is expected to span two levels inside the new terminal building, with space for more than 400 flyers. It will feature dining, working and relaxation areas — including a space Air France said it's reserving for "beauty treatments." Plus, the facility will include an exclusive dining area for meals whipped up by a "renowned French chef." How to access the Air France lounge at JFK Access will be limited to Air France and KLM passengers who book a seat in business class — or fly to Charles de Gaulle Airport (CDG) in Air France's luxe La Premier cabin on the Boeing 777-300ER. The new facility should certainly be a more worthy complement to the airline's most luxe premium seat in New York, which features on multiple daily flights from JFK. SkyTeam elites, too Plus, members who reach SkyTeam alliance Elite Plus status can enter when flying on an eligible itinerary. (For Delta SkyMiles members, that's Gold Medallion status and above). A brand-new Terminal One This new Air France lounge comes as part of the larger multibillion-dollar Terminal One that's currently in the final stages of construction. The new Terminal One is slated to replace the airport's existing Terminal 1 facility. And Air France is expected to be largest airline at the new terminal, thanks to its half-dozen daily roundtrips between JFK and Paris. "Air France's investment in our terminal's biggest lounge represents a strong vote of confidence in the seamless and modern travel experience we are building," new Terminal One CEO Jennifer Aument said in a statement Tuesday. The new building will also be home to a handful of other major global carriers, including Etihad, SAS, EVA and Turkish Airlines. Once the new facility opens, Qatar also plans to make the jump to the Terminal One from its current home in Terminal 8, the airport's main Oneworld alliance hub. Qatar is planning its own luxe club for the new JFK building — though it will be about half the size of Air France's new digs. In all, the new Terminal One is expected to house at least six lounges, including an arrivals lounge. How to book Air France flights with points and miles Travelers hoping to book Air France flights with miles have a wide range of options. Most major transferable credit card and rewards programs offer direct transfers to Flying Blue, the loyalty program it shares with sister carrier KLM. That includes 1:1 transfers from programs like American Express, Bilt Rewards and Chase. Plus, you can also book Air France flights using Delta SkyMiles, since the two carriers are partners. Bottom line Despite Tuesday's lounge news, the opening date for the new terminal itself has slipped a bit. A spokesperson for the new terminal tells TPG the facility is now on track to open during the first quarter of 2027. That's a delay from the previous 2026 timeline. "We want to ensure that all systems and processes are well-tested and prepared to deliver on our commitment to set a new standard in customer experience, from day one," the company said in a statement. Related reading:

item.title: Qantas’ A380 isn’t the newest way to fly — but kangaroo pajamas and an onboard lounge make it a treat
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy Score: 3.63
Qantas’ A380 isn’t the newest way to fly — but kangaroo pajamas and an onboard lounge make it a treat Quick take: Qantas continues to offer a solid business-class experience for long flights across the Pacific, but inflight Wi-Fi can't come soon enough. Pros - Seats are comfortable and have decent privacy. - Extensive menus offer diverse choices. - There's a fun onboard lounge space for passengers to enjoy. Cons - Award availability is very limited. - There's currently no Wi-Fi, so prepare to be offline. - The large cabin means meal service can take a while. The first Airbus A380 I ever flew was a Qantas aircraft way back in 2009, shortly after the airline started taking delivery of these double-decker jumbo jets. Since then, I've seen these planes evolve from newfangled novelties into long-haul workhorses not just for Qantas, but with several other carriers, too, including Emirates and Singapore Airlines. I have tracked its shifts from a time when it was hailed as the future of long-haul aviation, thanks to its enormous passenger capacity and flight range, to an uneconomic boondoggle that many thought was doomed to the fossil heap during the COVID-19 pandemic. The A380 endures, though, and Qantas currently has 10 of them in service, so it still holds a special place in my heart. I've been able to fly it dozens of times on many trips between the U.S. and Australia. My most recent flight was actually from Los Angeles to Melbourne at the kickoff of my honeymoon, when I got to experience Qantas business class for the first time in a few years. Here's how I booked my ticket and how the experience rates these days. How much does it cost to book Qantas business class? The cost of a Qantas long-haul, business-class ticket depends on the route, dates and whether you're flying round-trip or one-way. My one-way flight from Los Angeles International Airport (LAX) to Melbourne Airport (MEL) would have cost between $4,600 and $5,800 the week I flew. I was able to book an award ticket, though, with the option to use Alaska Airlines Atmos Rewards points or American Airlines AAdvantage miles. Here's a quick look at how my award ticket was priced across the two programs and Qantas' own Frequent Flyer program. | Frequent-flyer program | Miles and taxes | |---|---| | Alaska Airlines Atmos Rewards | 85,000 plus $36 | | American Airlines AAdvantage | 80,000 plus $24 | | Qantas Frequent Flyer | 151,800 plus $364 | Given the cost savings, I normally would have booked my ticket using American AAdvantage miles. However, I actually had many more Alaska Atmos Rewards points at the time, so I used those instead. Alaska Airlines is a 1:1 transfer partner of Bilt. You can also transfer Marriott Bonvoy points to Alaska at a 3:1 ratio. The best way to stock up on Alaska Airlines Atmos Rewards points quickly, however, is to apply for one of the following cobranded credit cards: - Atmos™ Rewards Ascent Visa Signature® credit card - Atmos™ Rewards Summit Visa Infinite® credit card - Atmos™ Rewards Visa Signature® Business Card If you do want to use American Airlines miles, the following cobranded credit cards are a great way to accrue miles quickly: The information for the AAdvantage Platinum Select has been collected independently by The Points Guy. The card details on this page have not been reviewed or provided by the card issuer. While the Qantas Frequent Flyer redemption rates were not a great option, I did consider it since Capital One was running a 20% transfer bonus to the program at the time; so, I would have only needed 121,440 Capital One miles. That said, although Capital One transfers to Qantas tend to be nearly instantaneous in my experience, I didn't want to chance the transfer taking too long and losing out on the award seat. That's because Qantas business-class award tickets available to book using partner miles are extremely rare. The airline seems to release a handful each month, typically in tranches (meaning a few award tickets become available on the same day for multiple dates over the following month or so). So if you find a seat, book it fast. I use tools like Seats.aero to monitor award tickets over multiple months at a time and get notifications when they become available, so I can book them quickly. Just one quick note on aircraft and routes: Qantas deploys both the A380 and the 787-9 on its Los Angeles-Melbourne route, and the airline will switch to solely 787-9s in October 2026. Checking into and boarding Qantas business class Qantas long-haul business-class passengers can enjoy the following priority services at the airport. | Priority check-in | Yes | |---|---| | Luggage allowance | Two checked bags up to 70 pounds (32 kg) each | | Lounge access | Yes | | Does the airline participate in TSA PreCheck? | Yes | | Priority boarding | Yes | My Qantas flight was scheduled to depart at 9:50 p.m. from LAX's Tom Bradley International Terminal. I arrived at the airport at 7 p.m., when the departure hall was pretty quiet, and there were only a few passengers in the dedicated business- and first-class lines. There were no lines at security, and thanks to TSA PreCheck, I was airside within just a few minutes of arriving at the airport. Qantas business-class passengers can use the Oneworld lounge on the fifth floor — a massive space with a capacity of nearly 600 guests and open to premium passengers from various airlines, including British Airways and Cathay Pacific. When I flew, the lounge had also converted a space near the bar by the entrance into a makeshift first-class dining room since the airline's permanent first-class lounge was under renovation. My flight departed from the 200 gates in the terminal's western concourse, which is a brisk 15-minute walk from the lounge, so I gave myself plenty of time to get over there. Boarding was right on time at 9:05 p.m. How comfortable is Qantas business class? Qantas' long-haul fleet consists of Airbus A330s, A380s and Boeing 787-9 Dreamliners. Its first A350-1000 was recently delivered and will be equipped with all-new seating options for the ultra-long-haul "Project Sunrise" flights the jet will operate. On the other three aircraft types, however, the business-class seats are all based on the popular Thompson Aero Vantage XL model, which are forward-facing in a staggered 1-2-1 pattern. The 15-year-old A380 operating my flight had the tail number VH-OQK and was named after Australian aviation pioneers (and brothers) John and Reginald Duigan. Here's a snapshot of its business-class layout and dimensions. | Number of seats | 70 | |---|---| | Cabin layout | 1-2-1 | | Seat recline | 80 inches fully flat | | Seat width | 21 inches (24 in lie-flat mode) | | Screen size | 15.5 inches | The business-class section on Qantas' A380s took up nearly the entire upper deck, with a smaller cabin of just 20 seats up front and a larger cabin with 50 more seats behind the galley and lavatory. The seats were in a staggered 1-2-1 configuration, so every passenger had direct aisle access. The single seats on the sides were alternately closer or farther from the window due to the placement of a wide armrest. Those in the middle had a wide armrest between them as well as a raisable shield, so there was a fair amount of privacy; however, there were no sliding doors, which are becoming more popular (and which you'll see on Qantas' forthcoming A350s). The gap between the armrest and the preceding seat shell — in other words, the exit from the seat — was 10 inches. This doesn't sound like a lot, but it is still more than you find in some other similar fixtures. | Best seats for solo travelers | Odd-numbered A and K seats in the forward cabin, even ones in the back cabin | |---|---| | Best seats for couples | Any E and F seats | The airline's A380s underwent a refurbishment starting in 2019 that was extended due to the coronavirus pandemic, so these pods were the latest versions from the airline's industrial design partner, David Caon. The seats had a sharp aesthetic with charcoal-gray leather accents and upholstery with silvery dotted patterning, brushed metal shells and dark faux-wood paneling. The seat cushions were 18 inches wide at the shoulders, but I measured the distance between armrests at the hips to be 24 inches, so they feel very roomy. The wider armrest had some shelving for small items, plus a hook for headphones, a water bottle holder and a small reading light. This was also where I found a universal power plug and a USB-A port (no USB-C, I'm afraid). There was a panel with seat controls that included preset positions for takeoff and landing, lounging and lie-flat mode, as well as buttons to control the individual parts of the seat; I found this handy for getting into a just-right position. I could also control the ambient seat lighting and the small reading light using buttons on the panel, and I could illuminate a "Do Not Disturb" indicator if I wanted the crew to leave me be while I rested. There wasn't much other storage to speak of since I didn't have one of the single side seats; those seats actually had large bins set against the window for storing amenity kits, bedding and other belongings. The seat's tray table popped out horizontally from the wide armrest and measured about 11 inches by 19 inches — plenty of room for my laptop. In lie-flat mode, the seat stretched to an 80-inch bed, and I found it comfortable to sleep in various positions. The foot cubby was 14 inches wide at its mouth and 11 inches tall, so folks with bigger feet might find it a bit cramped. Each seat had two individual overhead air nozzles, which made it easy to control the temperature in my area, though the crew kept the cabin pleasantly cool throughout the flight. There were two lavatories in the center galley section between the two business-class cabins and two more behind the larger business-class cabin. Although the restroom-to-passenger ratio was pretty good, there were lines after meals. The crew kept them very clean throughout the flight, though. One of the things I like best about flying Qantas business and first class aboard the A380 is the swanky little lounge at the front of the upper deck for premium passengers. It features a long banquette with seat belts and a self-serve area to one side of the staircase leading down to the lower deck, and two tables with plugs and seat belts to the other, so you can gather with your travel companions for a quick hang. Amenities in Qantas business class Each business-class seat was provisioned with a bed set that included a lightweight duvet, a seat cover and a medium-size pillow. I found the inclusion of a seat cover especially nice, as it meant I didn't have to sleep directly on a surface countless other passengers had sat on. I also found a little amenity kit from Australian clothing and leather brand R.M. Williams, which was a nice Aussie touch. Inside, it included: - A bamboo toothbrush - Toothpaste - Eye mask - Warm socks - Ear plugs - Grown Alchemist vanilla-orange peel hand cream - Grown Alchemist vanilla-watermelon lip balm - Grown Alchemist geranium and camellia day cream Shortly after boarding, flight attendants came through offering passengers pajamas, and though a small-medium would have fit me (I'm 5 feet, 8 inches), I asked for a large-extra large because I like them roomy. The seat's entertainment screen was 15 1/2 inches across diagonally and had dozens of new movies and TV shows, including "The Devil Wears Prada 2," "Hoppers," and "The Super Mario Galaxy Movie." The screen tilted up and down to make viewing easier, whether sitting upright or reclined. The airline provided basic headphones that plugged into a jack near the USB port, but there was no way to connect my own headphones to the system via Bluetooth. Unfortunately, Qantas does not have Wi-Fi on its A380s, but the airline is starting to equip them with the service, with rollout across all 10 expected to be completed by mid-2027. How was the food in Qantas business class? When I boarded, I found both the main menu and breakfast menu waiting at my seat. Unlike some other airlines, Qantas does not offer a preorder option for its regular menus, though those with special dietary needs can order ahead. As folks got settled in, flight attendants passed through the cabin with trays of Jacquart Mosaique Brut Champagne and water. About 30 minutes into the flight, meal service started with a choice of beverages and an "aperitivo" of mixed nuts served in a little Noritake porcelain bowl. The main meal was served between all on one tray — probably due to the late hour of the flight and the fact that most passengers wanted to get to bed. Flight attendants were quick, but given the size of the cabin, meal service started about an hour into the flight and lasted about 90 minutes. It included a small green salad with vinaigrette and a choice of the following from the menu designed by the airline's chef partner, Neil Perry: - Brassica and pea soup with mint and pea tendrils - Gnocchi with roasted pumpkin, asparagus, sage, hazelnut and ricotta - Seared halibut with braised beans, kale, calamari, capers, olives and almond salsa - Spicy kaffir lime chicken curry with stir-fried green beans, red chili and jasmine rice - Braised beef cheek with slow-roasted baby sweet potatoes, creamed silverbeet and black pepper sour cream I ordered the chicken curry, and it was fantastic. The portion was hearty, and the sauce was flavorful but light, while the meat turned out juicy and tender. To finish, folks could choose from a selection of cheeses, including Manchego and Fourme d'Ambert, tiramisu, ice cream, or seasonal fruit. I ordered the latter for a light finish to my meal. Throughout the rest of the flight, folks could order a few small dishes on demand, including crudites with hummus, a chicken-cheese sandwich with roasted peppers and zucchini, cookies, chocolate bars, mixed nuts, potato chips and fruit. The wines on offer were not listed on the menu, but included a chardonnay from Victoria and a sauvignon blanc-semillon blend from Western Australia, plus a Shiraz from the Barossa and a pinot noir. There were also various drinks and spirits on hand, including Four Pillars gin and Bundaberg dark rum, as well as a selection of Australian beers. Flight attendants often came through during and after meal service to see if passengers wanted refills. About two hours before landing, the cabin lighting gradually got brighter, and flight attendants began serving breakfast to passengers who were awake. I slept a little longer and was offered breakfast when I got up, about 75 minutes before landing. The crew could offer this slightly staggered service because passengers fill out their menu cards earlier in the flight, making it easier to assemble trays. Passengers could choose from a selection of juices, coffee and tea, along with food items like yogurt, fruit salad, muesli, toast, croissants and mains that included: - Buttermilk pancakes with raspberry compote, yogurt and hazelnut praline - Poached eggs with mixed mushrooms, asparagus and Manchego cheese on toast - Scrambled eggs with grilled applewood bacon, balsamic roasted tomatoes and sauteed kale and spinach I got a coffee with milk and sugar, which came out hot and strong, plus a healthy green juice and the scrambled eggs. The portion was substantial, and the eggs came out well — firm and slightly fluffy. We were landing in Melbourne at around 6 a.m., so I only ate sparingly since I had the whole day ahead of me to explore the city's food scene. All told, the meals were well executed, nicely presented and served efficiently, so passengers could maximize their rest and relaxation. Would you recommend Qantas business class? The main drawback to flying Qantas across the Pacific is the lack of Wi-Fi. So if you're traveling for business and need to stay online, that's a real consideration. Hopefully, that will resolve over the coming months as the airline installs Wi-Fi across its A380 fleet. Other than that, the airline remains one of my favorite ways to fly long-haul. The crew is friendly and polished, and the seats look sleek and provide enough privacy that the lack of a closing door doesn't feel significant. Plus, the meal service and entertainment options are plentiful. I do wish the airline would release more saver-level award availability to partner programs like American Airlines AAdvantage and Alaska Airlines Atmos Rewards. But if you have some flexibility in your schedule, you should be able to find a few seats each month, and tools like Seats.aero come in handy for doing so. As for me, you'll find me hanging out in my kangaroo-emblazoned Qantas pajamas plotting my next flight aboard the Australian carrier. Related reading:

item.title: Deal alert: Points and miles travel deals for September 2026
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy Score: 3.59
Deal alert: Points and miles travel deals for September 2026 Editor's Note From bonus points on your next hotel stay to sales on award tickets, we're always looking for travel deals that help you earn more points and miles and redeem them for maximum value. In other words, we want to help you book the vacation of your dreams. This time around, we've got some valuable new perks on an under-the-radar airline credit card and a offer that could save you $200 on a ski trip. Delta SkyMiles and World of Hyatt members can earn more rewards with this exciting new partnership. And don't forget to activate your Q3 bonus categories on this fan-favorite credit card. Each week, we help our readers by rounding up promotions so they don't have to scour the internet for the best reward redemptions and offers. This includes everything from frequent flyer programs and hotel rewards programs to credit card offers and rental car deals. Here's our latest list of noteworthy new points and miles promotions for September. Airline loyalty program promotions (September 2026) Airline loyalty programs can offer trip discounts on specific dates, the opportunity to earn more points or miles for future travel and exclusive deals to accumulate points or miles toward elite status. Below is one of the best offers we found for September. Save money and earn more miles on flights to Asia With Cathay Pacific's 80th anniversary sale, Asia Miles members can score cash discounts and bonus miles on flights to Asia. Use promo code CX80HKUS to save $80 per ticket to Hong Kong or code CX80US for $88 off per ticket to Asia and beyond, including economy, premium economy and business class. This offer ends Sept. 23, but limited quantities are available on a first-come, first-served basis, so start making your plans soon. The airline is also offering various other rewards, including up to 1,946 bonus miles to new members who join and take a Cathay Pacific flight from the U.S. or Canada to most Cathay destinations worldwide. Register and book by Sept. 15 for travel through Dec. 10. Earn up to 14k bonus miles on a single flight If you're planning a multi-city or round-the-world trip, this offer from Qatar Airways Privilege Club could come in handy. Now through Sept. 18, you can save 20% and earn up to a whopping 14,000 bonus Avios on eligible flights out of the U.K. or Europe. That's 10,000 bonus points when you book with code SEPTPC26, 2,000 more for your first eligible online booking and another 2,000 if you're a new member. Plus, you'll be allowed one free date change on eligible bookings made during the offer period (fare difference may apply). Travel must be completed by Dec. 10, 2026, for one-way flights or May 31, 2027, for round-trip flights. Related: How to choose an airline credit card Hotel loyalty program promotions (September 2026) Hotel loyalty programs regularly offer discounted award stays and new ways to earn extra points. Here are some September deals to consider when booking your next stay. Double your Hyatt points at Thompson hotels World of Hyatt is celebrating 25 years of its elegant Thompson brand with bonus points. Members can double their base earnings at Thompson properties this fall when they register, book through the World of Hyatt app and stay by Nov. 10. Even better, you can take advantage of this promotion multiple times up to a cap of 30,000 bonus points. That's worth an impressive $495 based on TPG's Sept. 2026 valuations. Rack up bonus points with two Marriott deals Dreaming of a sunny getaway this fall or winter? You can score 20,000 bonus points — worth $150 by our valuations — on a vacation package of three-plus nights in Hawaii or Mexico through Vacations by Marriott Bonvoy. Book by Sept. 30, 2026, for travel through March 31, 2027. The Marriott deals don't end there. Bonvoy members can also earn up to 4,500 bonus points per qualifying stay: 1,500 bonus points when you stay two or more nights, plus an additional 3,000 bonus points at resort properties. Register by Nov. 13 for stays from Sept. 22 through Nov. 22. Be sure to check your Amex account before you book, as we've seen some targeted Amex Offers to help you save on Marriott purchases. Related: Best hotel credit cards Rental car promotions (September 2026) Summer may be almost over, but that doesn't mean you can't take an epic road trip. This rental car deal can help you save this fall. Get your fifth day free with Hertz Hertz is offering a fifth day free when you book an SUV or minivan for 4-27 days at participating Hertz locations in the U.S. This applies only to the base rate; taxes and fees are excluded. Book with promo code 212109 and pick up your vehicle by Dec. 31. Don't forget to stack this deal with any perks or elite status you may have at Hertz through your credit card. Credit card promotions (September 2026) Card issuers offer deals and discounts on a wide range of products, from airfare to dining. Here are some of the offers we've rounded up this week. Note that these are targeted, so they may or may not be available on your account. You must activate these offers on your card and use the enrolled card to make the purchase in order to earn bonus rewards. Targeted Amex Offer at Marriott If a Marriott stay is in your future, check your Amex account. Targeted cardholders can earn $200 back when they spend $450 or more at participating Marriott Bonvoy properties in the U.S., Canada, Mexico and the Caribbean by Nov. 30 — potentially saving you up to 44%. Targeted Amex Offer on cruises Ready to sail away on your next adventure? This Amex Offer, which we spotted on the American Express® Gold Card, could help you save at Holland America. Book online, by phone at 1-877-932-4259, or through a Holland America travel advisor by Oct. 22. Targeted Amex Offer at Europcar If you're targeted, this Europcar offer could save you money on a rental car. Earn $50 back when you spend at least $250 on prepaid Europcar rentals booked online by Oct. 21. Related: The ultimate guide to saving money with Amex Offers Ongoing travel deals In addition to these new offers, many others from previous weeks are still available: - If you live in Washington State, you can earn one Delta SkyMile for every passing yard the Seahawks complete this season. Sign up to start earning. - Until Sept. 30, earn 25 AAdvantage bonus miles for every dollar you give online on donations of $25 or more. You can double your bonus miles by paying with an American Airlines cobranded card. - Earn 3,000 bonus World of Hyatt points per stay — up to 30,000 total — when you spend at least three nights at participating Hyatt Place and Hyatt Select hotels in the U.S., Canada, the Caribbean and Latin America. Register first, then book and complete your stay(s) by Sept. 30. - Earn 2,000 bonus Marriott Bonvoy points per night, up to 6,000 total, at 60 participating properties across Thailand. Book with code "S2449" and stay by Sept. 30. - Save up to 25% on award flights to and from Europe with Flying Blue's September Promo Rewards. Book by Sept. 30, 2026, and travel by Feb. 28, 2027. - Through Sept. 30, you can double your Hyatt points on eligible dine-in and takeaway spending at participating Hyatt restaurants and bars across Asia Pacific with this promotion. - Earn 5,000 bonus points when you complete a stay at any Bonvoy hotel by Sept. 30. Link your accounts and register for the promotion here. - With this lucrative World of Hyatt promotion, you can earn a Category 1-4 Free Night Award for every three nights you stay across Latin America and the Caribbean — up to five free nights total. Register by Sept. 30, 2026, then complete your stay(s) at participating hotels between Jan. 1 and March 31, 2027. - Marriott Bonvoy is offering a whopping 50,000 bonus points per stay, plus complimentary breakfast for up to two guests, for guests who visit the luxurious Ritz-Carlton Kyoto by Sept. 30. Just be sure to book with the promo code, which can be found here. - New members who join Chevron Texaco Rewards by Sept. 30 can save $1 per gallon on their first five fill-ups. - Earn 2,000 bonus Bonvoy points per night, up to 10,000 per stay, at eligible Marriott Homes & Villas vacation rentals. Book and complete your rental by Oct. 31 (blackout dates apply). - Get a 15% points rebate on stays at World of Hyatt's Under Canvas locations. Register by Nov. 30 for stays through Dec. 1. - Earn double Bonvoy elite night credits on vacation rentals through Homes & Villas by Marriott when you stay at least two nights by Dec. 15. Plus, if you stay during Thanksgiving week (Nov. 21-30), you'll earn double points toward your next free night on top of the bonus elite night credits. Register and book by Sept. 30. - New members of the Alaska Airlines Atmos Rewards program can save up to $50 on their next flight simply by joining the program by Dec. 31. U.S. residents outside Alaska, California and Hawaii can register here for their discount code; residents of Alaska, California and Hawaii can register here. - Earn 5,000 bonus Hyatt points on each stay of five-plus nights at participating Hyatt House and Hyatt Studios properties. Register, book and stay by Dec. 31. - Best Western is awarding double points at more than 4,000 participating hotels worldwide with this promo. Register first, then book and stay by Dec. 31. - If you're targeted for Hilton's "Stay More, Earn More" offer, you can earn up to 15,000 bonus points in total on your next five stays. Check to see if you're targeted and register here by Dec. 31, then complete your stay(s) within six months of registration. Targeted Amex Offers - Get $100 back when spending $500 or more on a Sixt rental booked online by Sept. 15. - Earn a $40 statement credit after you make a qualifying purchase of $250 or more at viator.com. This offer expires Sept. 30. - Get a $350 statement credit after spending a minimum of $1,000 in qualifying purchases at participating Homes & Villas by Marriott Bonvoy properties. Book here by Sept. 30. - Earn a $15 statement credit on a pet boarding purchase of $75 or more at meowtel.com. Book on the Wyndham website, and complete your purchase by Oct. 27. - Earn $200 back when you spend at least $1,000 in one or more qualifying purchases online by Oct. 31. Excludes Canada locations. - Earn a one-time $100 statement credit when you spend a minimum of $500 at participating Hyatt properties in the U.S., the Caribbean and Latin America by Nov. 15. - Get $50 back on a single purchase of $250 or more with Italo Treno when you book online or through the Italo Treno mobile app by Dec. 27. - Earn a $30 statement credit after spending $150 or more on a Turo rental in the U.S. or Canada.
